highlights: # Kimi-maker Moonshot AI targets $2 billion in annual revenue. One of China’s most prominent AI labs, Moonshot AI, believes it can turn its popular open-weight model into serious sales growth. On Friday, Bloomberg reported that the lab is targeting $2 billion in annualized revenue by the end of the year, double the company’s reported revenue run rate for August. It’s an aggressive goal that reflects the success of the company’s K3 model since its release this summer. Moonshot’s projected revenue is still dwarfed by that of OpenAI and Anthropic, which recent reports put at $40 billion and $65 billion respectively. The rising projections show there’s still money to be made from open-weight AI models, even if they’re not as lucrative as closed-weight frontier models. Earlier this week, Anthropic accused the company of a long-running model distillation campaign that routed nearly 300,000 requests from Kimi directly to Claude Opus, effectively serving Opus in place of Kimi’s own models.

latest.summary: Image 1: THE JournalWhere AI and ed tech meet K–12 innovation. *   OpenAI says an internal AI system produced a proposed solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, while Anthropic...
highlights: Image 1: THE JournalWhere AI and ed tech meet K–12 innovation. *   OpenAI says an internal AI system produced a proposed solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, while Anthropic has reported separate advances in research mathematics and formal proof generation. *   Formal verification tools such as Lean could become increasingly important as AI-generated research scales, because the ability to produce mathematical results may soon outpace the human capacity to check them. OpenAIhas announced what it says is an AI-generated solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of mathematics' seven Millennium Prize Problems. OpenAI's proposed proof argues that an initially smooth fluid can develop a singularity, essentially a mathematical breakdown in which velocity grows without bound in finite time. The company released both the proof and a computer-checkable formalization written in the Lean proof assistant. A proof of a Millennium Prize Problem does not become established mathematics because an AI company publishes it.

Guo also highlighted similarities in the outer space-inspired design of OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra web page and the website for JoyIn's Aether model that he claimed was released two months ago. latest.title: OpenAI pulls out of Caltech math hackathon after mathematicians issue open letter criticizing AI math 'slop' - Business Insider
latest.summary: The latest math problem OpenAI is trying to solve is a bunch of angry mathematicians. A researcher at OpenAI said on Thursday that the ChatGPT maker is no longer sponsoring Caltech's "math hackathon,"...
highlights: The latest math problem OpenAI is trying to solve is a bunch of angry mathematicians. A researcher at OpenAI said on Thursday that the ChatGPT maker is no longer sponsoring Caltech's "math hackathon," an event where participants use large language models to solve research problems. OpenAI's exit follows an open letter released on Wednesday from current and former Caltech mathematicians, who said the event, which is sponsored by AI companies, "is likely to have destructive impacts for the mathematical community.". "We recognize that the rapid progress of AI in mathematics is disruptive," Dan Roberts, OpenAI's research lead, said on X. At issue, according to the mathematicians, is the manner in which AI companies claim to solve outstanding theoretical problems using their models and then leave practical applications and proofs to actual researchers. "It's our first time running an event at this scale, and we are grateful for all the feedback we have received.".

highlights: # OpenAI Gives US Agencies 50% Off Models, Ending $1 Per Year Deal. ## Takeaways by Bloomberg AISubscribe. OpenAI is ending a pilot program that allowed government agencies to use its models for only $1 per year and moving to a usage-based pricing system that will give federal workers access to the technology at a 50% discount from standard prices, according to a statement from the General Services Administration. In a push to drive adoption of its models in August of last year, OpenAI joined the GSA’s marketplace, a hub called OneGov that allows federal agencies to buy AI software at scale. The first year’s negotiated terms of $1 per year represented the steepest tech discount the government’s central purchasing arm had ever negotiated, Bloomberg previously reported. During that time, according to the GSA, 3.5 million federal employees have been able to access OpenAI’s ChatGPT, generating $1.4 billion in cost savings from it and other AI models.

The rupture is a symptom of the rapid changes taking place in the field due to AI advancements and what Strogatz—who cowrote Big Math, a book about how math is slipping away from human understanding that will be out in November—describes as corporate labs’ race to grab headlines ahead of blockbuster IPOs. Last week, Anthropic said Claude had proved 29,500 small theorems while formalizing an existing proof of the infamous Fermat’s Last Theorem—a project other mathematicians had been working on for years.
